_meta.notes: Country-scoped curated nodes; link via relationships during ingest.

910.name: San Rock Art and Early Inhabitants
910.label: Event
910.description: San hunter-gatherers inhabit the Maloti-Drakensberg mountains for tens of thousands of years, leaving one of the richest rock-art traditions in southern Africa.

910.name: Stone Age Highland Settlements
910.label: Event
910.description: Middle and Later Stone Age tools found in rock shelters across the Lesotho highlands; evidence of seasonal transhumance patterns.

910.name: San Rock Art of the Maloti-Drakensberg
910.label: Event
910.description: Thousands of polychrome rock paintings depicting eland hunts, rain-making rituals, and therianthropic (half-human/half-animal) trance figures; among the finest in the world.

920.name: Bantu Migration and Early Sotho Communities
920.label: Event
920.description: Bantu-speaking peoples settle the region; Sotho-Tswana communities develop distinct cultural and political identities in the highlands.

920.name: Early Bantu Settlement
920.label: Event
920.description: Bantu-speaking farmers arrive from the north, introducing iron-working, sorghum cultivation, and cattle keeping; interaction with and gradual displacement of San populations.

920.name: Formation of Sotho Chiefdoms
920.label: Event
920.description: Sotho-speaking groups (Bakwena, Bafokeng, Bataung, Basia) establish chiefdoms in the highland valleys; cattle-based economy; stone-walled settlement sites.

930.name: Moshoeshoe I and the Basotho Nation
930.label: Event
930.description: Moshoeshoe I (c.1786–1870), one of Africa's greatest statesmen, unites diverse refugees of the Difaqane into the Basotho nation from his mountain fortress of Thaba Bosiu.

930.name: Moshoeshoe's Rise and Thaba Bosiu
930.label: Event
930.description: Born Lepoqo of the Bamokoteli; renamed Moshoeshoe ('the Shaver'); moves followers to impregnable flat-topped mountain of Thaba Bosiu in 1824.

930.name: Basotho Nation Formation during Difaqane
930.label: Event
930.description: Moshoeshoe shelters and absorbs refugees from Zulu, Ndebele, and Griqua raids; builds a new multi-clan nation through diplomacy, cattle-loaning (mafisa), and strategic marriages.

940.name: Basutoland Protectorate
940.label: Event
940.description: British Basutoland protectorate preserved from South African incorporation; the Gun War demonstrates Basotho resistance; migrant labour to South African mines reshapes society.

940.name: The Gun War (1880–1881)
940.label: Event
940.description: Basotho refuse Cape Colony's attempt to disarm them; successful resistance leads to direct British imperial control rather than Cape administration; only southern African people never fully conquered.

940.name: British Colonial Administration
940.label: Event
940.description: Indirect rule through paramount chief and district chiefs; Basutoland National Council established 1903; deliberate underdevelopment; territory remains surrounded by South Africa.

950.name: Independence and Early Political Struggles
950.label: Event
950.description: Lesotho gains independence in 1966; Chief Leabua Jonathan's authoritarian rule; conflict between BNP and BCP; South African economic and military pressure.

950.name: Lesotho Independence 1966
950.label: Event
950.description: Constitutional development; Basutoland Congress Party (BCP) vs Basotho National Party (BNP); independence on 4 October 1966 under King Moshoeshoe II and PM Leabua Jonathan.

950.name: Leabua Jonathan's Authoritarian Rule
950.label: Event
950.description: Jonathan suspends constitution after losing 1970 election; declares state of emergency; Lesotho Liberation Army insurgency; South African blockade 1986 leads to military coup.

950.name: Military Rule and Democratic Transition
950.label: Event
950.description: Military junta 1986–1993; democratic transition; King Moshoeshoe II's exile and return; political instability continues.

950.name: Military Junta 1986–1993
950.label: Event
950.description: General Lekhanya overthrows Jonathan; restores executive powers to King Moshoeshoe II then exiles him; Major General Ramaema takes over 1991; transition to elections.

950.name: 1993 Democratic Elections
950.label: Event
950.description: BCP wins all 65 seats; factional politics; King Moshoeshoe II returns and dies in car accident 1996; King Letsie III ascends; 1998 election dispute triggers SADC intervention.

960.name: Modern Lesotho: Mountain Kingdom Challenges
960.label: Event
960.description: Lesotho navigates post-intervention reforms, the Highlands Water Project, HIV/AIDS crisis, political instability, and economic dependence on South Africa.

960.name: Lesotho Highlands Water Project
960.label: Event
960.description: Massive engineering project supplying water to South Africa's Gauteng province; Phase I completed 2003; Phase II (Polihali Dam) under construction; royalties fund Lesotho's budget.

960.name: Political Instability and Attempted Coups
960.label: Event
960.description: PM Tom Thabane's coalition politics; Lieutenant General Kamoli's 2014 attempted coup; SADC mediates; Thabane charged with murder of ex-wife; multiple snap elections.
